description: TalosCluster is one Talos cluster: what its members share, and the observed state of the cluster they form.

fields.name: spec
fields.description: TalosClusterSpec is what every member of one Talos cluster shares. The cluster name is the object's metadata.name.

fields.name: certSANs
fields.description: CertSANs are extra names the Kubernetes API server and the Talos API certificates must be valid for, beyond the endpoint, the VIP and the node addresses Talos adds on its own.

fields.name: controlPlane
fields.description: ControlPlane carries the settings only control-plane members render.

fields.name: allowScheduling
fields.description: AllowScheduling lets ordinary workloads run on control-plane nodes (the control-plane NoSchedule taint is not rendered).

fields.name: vip
fields.description: VIP is a shared address the control-plane members announce over layer 2 (Talos' Layer2VIPConfig). Each control-plane node carries it on the link whose static address shares a subnet with it.

fields.name: credentials
fields.description: Credentials sets the lifetime of the admin credentials the operator publishes, and whether it also publishes a read-only talosconfig.

fields.name: readerTalosconfig
fields.description: ReaderTalosconfig also publishes <cluster>-talosconfig-reader: a talosconfig with the os:reader role, for monitoring, which can read but not change a machine.

fields.name: ttl
fields.description: TTL is how long a published admin kubeconfig and talosconfig are valid. A credential is minted again once less than a third of it is left. Default 24h, at most 720h (30 days): a longer one stays valid long after the person who copied it has gone.

validations.message: ttl must be at most 720h: a published credential cannot be revoked short of a CA rotation

fields.name: endpoint
fields.description: Endpoint is the Kubernetes API URL every member enrolls against and the admin kubeconfig names: the control-plane VIP or a DNS name for it, with the port (https://10.77.0.10:6443).

fields.name: kubernetesVersion
fields.description: KubernetesVersion is the Kubernetes release the control plane runs.

fields.name: network
fields.description: Network is the cluster's pod and service networking.

fields.name: cni
fields.description: CNI selects the pod network plugin. Empty means flannel.

validations.message: urls are required with name custom and refused otherwise

fields.name: name
fields.description: CNIName selects the pod network plugin Talos deploys.

fields.name: urls
fields.description: URLs are the manifests a custom CNI is installed from.

fields.name: podSubnets
fields.description: PodSubnets are the pod CIDRs, primary family first. Empty selects Talos' default for the endpoint's address family.

fields.name: serviceSubnets
fields.description: ServiceSubnets are the service CIDRs, primary family first. Empty selects Talos' default for the endpoint's address family.

fields.name: patches
fields.description: Patches apply to every node, in order, after the operator's own rendering and before the node's patches.

validations.message: exactly one of inline or configMapRef

fields.name: configMapRef
fields.description: ConfigMapRef reads the patch from a ConfigMap key.

fields.name: key
fields.description: The key in the object's data.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the object.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: The namespace of the object.

fields.name: inline
fields.description: Inline is the patch text.

fields.name: registryMirrors
fields.description: RegistryMirrors redirect image pulls, one entry per upstream registry. A site without internet access needs them before the first node installs, which is why they live here rather than in a patch someone has to remember.

fields.name: endpoints
fields.description: Endpoints are the mirror URLs, tried in order.

fields.name: registry
fields.description: Registry is the upstream registry host the mirror stands in for (docker.io, ghcr.io, factory.talos.dev), or "*" for every registry.

fields.name: schematic
fields.description: Schematic is the installer image customization every node uses unless it sets its own (a node's schematic replaces this one, it does not merge with it).

fields.name: customization
fields.description: SchematicCustomization holds the image customization knobs.

fields.name: extraKernelArgs
fields.description: ExtraKernelArgs append to the image's kernel command line, for example where to put the console (console=ttyS0, what the BMC's serial-over-LAN shows). Do not add talos.config=metal-iso: the operator adds it to the boot medium itself, and the installed system must not carry it.

fields.name: systemExtensions
fields.description: SystemExtensions bakes extensions into the image.

fields.name: officialExtensions
fields.description: OfficialExtensions are siderolabs/* extension names (siderolabs/drbd).

fields.name: secretsRef
fields.description: SecretsRef names the Secret holding the cluster's Talos secrets bundle under key secrets.yaml, as `talosctl gen secrets` writes it. A person generates the bundle once and commits it sealed; the operator only reads it. Every certificate and key in a rendered config, and the kubeconfig and talosconfig the operator publishes, derive from it.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the object.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: The namespace of the object.

fields.name: talosVersion
fields.description: TalosVersion is the Talos release the cluster runs. It selects the configuration contract the render targets and the installer image tag, so it must match what the machines boot. Talos v1.14 or later.

fields.name: status
fields.description: TalosClusterStatus is observed: whether etcd was bootstrapped, whether the Kubernetes API answers, how many members are Ready, and where the admin credentials derived from the secrets bundle were published.

validations.message: bootstrappedAt is write-once: a cluster that was bootstrapped stays bootstrapped

fields.name: bootstrappedAt
fields.description: BootstrappedAt is when the operator first observed this cluster's etcd running (or its Kubernetes API answering). It is the one remembered fact in this status: once set the operator never bootstraps the cluster again, so that a cluster whose control planes all lost their etcd data is restored by a person instead of silently started empty (Bootstrapped=False, reason EtcdDataLost). Write-once; starting over means deleting and re-creating the TalosCluster.

fields.name: conditions
fields.description: Conditions: Bootstrapped and Available; VersionsSupported (the Kubernetes version against the Talos version), VersionsCurrent (what the machines and the API run against the spec) and SecretsBundleHeld (an edited secrets bundle the machines do not run yet).

fields.name: lastTransitionTime
fields.description: The time of the last change of the status.

fields.name: message
fields.description: A message for people about the last change. It can be empty.

fields.name: observedGeneration
fields.description: The generation of the object that the condition is for. A lower value than metadata.generation shows an old condition.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: A word in CamelCase that tells why the condition has its status.

fields.name: status
fields.description: The status of the condition: True, False or Unknown.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The type of the condition.

fields.name: controlPlanes
fields.description: ControlPlanes and Workers count the TalosNodes that name this cluster and that a machine is handed (a Host's spec.os names them); the Ready counts are the ones whose Ready condition is True. A TalosNode with no machine yet, or one being removed, is counted in UnassignedNodes instead: it is not a member, so it does not hold Available at False.

fields.name: credentialsExpireAt
fields.description: CredentialsExpireAt is when the first of the published credentials expires. The operator mints new ones well before; a time in the past means it could not.

fields.name: kubeconfigSecretRef
fields.description: KubeconfigSecretRef points at the Secret (key kubeconfig) holding an admin kubeconfig minted from the bundle's Kubernetes CA.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the object.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: The namespace of the object.

fields.name: kubernetesVersion
fields.description: KubernetesVersion is the version the Kubernetes API reports, empty while it does not answer.

fields.name: readerTalosconfigSecretRef
fields.description: ReaderTalosconfigSecretRef points at the os:reader talosconfig, when spec.credentials.readerTalosconfig asks for one.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the object.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: The namespace of the object.

fields.name: talosconfigSecretRef
fields.description: TalosconfigSecretRef points at the Secret (key talosconfig) holding an admin talosconfig minted from the bundle's Talos CA, with every control-plane address as an endpoint.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the object.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: The namespace of the object.

fields.name: unassignedNodes
fields.description: UnassignedNodes counts the TalosNodes that name this cluster but run on no machine: not handed to a Host yet, or being removed.
